item.title: Amazon, Walmart Face Data Requests in DOJ Beef Antitrust Probe
item.description: The US Justice Department expanded its antitrust inquiry of the meatpacking industry by demanding information on surging beef prices from eight major food retailers, including Amazon.com Inc., Costco Wholesale Corp. and Walmart Inc.
item.dc:creator: Leah Nylen and Ilena Peng

item.title: Dell Rises on Sales Outlook Boost
item.description: Dell raised its outlook for a fifth straight quarter as demand for AI and traditional servers continues to surge. Portia Capital Management President Michelle Connell explains why she sees more upside for Dell, where the next winners could emerge across the AI hardware stack, and how supply constraints are reshaping the semiconductor race. She joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Napster Shifts Course to Penny-a-Minute AI Agents Via Microsoft
item.description: Napster, the former music-streaming platform, is betting on low-cost AI agents as its path back to success.
item.dc:creator: Ed Ludlow

item.title: Iran-linked Hackers Hit 100 American Water Utilities
item.description: EPA giving away $11 million to boost water systems cybersecurity
item.dc:creator: Ryan Gallagher

item.title: Dell Boosts Sales Outlook by $25 Billion
item.description: Dell shares jumped after the company boosted its annual sales forecast by $25 billion in a further sign of surging demand for servers to run artificial intelligence tasks. Revenue in the fiscal year ending in January 2027 will be about $192 billion, including $74 billion from the sale of AI servers, the Texas-based company said Tuesday in a statement. That’s up from an outlook in May of about $167 billion and topped analysts’ average projection of $173.8 billion, according to data compiled by Bloomberg. The AI server forecast represents a threefold increase over the prior year. This is the fifth straight quarter that Dell’s fiscal year revenue outlook topped estimates. Bloomberg Intelligence Senior Hardware and Networking Analyst said memory inflation is factoring into their guidance. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Uber’s $15 Billion Delivery Hero Takeover Gains Board Backing
item.description: Delivery Hero SE’s board voted to accept a takeover offer from Uber Technologies Inc., moving the nearly $15 billion deal for the German delivery platform another step toward completion.
item.dc:creator: Amy Thomson

item.title: NYSE Used Anthropic’s Project Glasswing to Find Cyber Flaws
item.description: The New York Stock Exchange used Anthropic PBC’s Project Glasswing to find and fix vulnerabilities in its cyber security systems, its president, Lynn Martin, told Congress.
item.dc:creator: Caitlin Reilly

item.title: How Microsoft Is Helping Napster Reinvent Itself
item.description: John Acunto, Napster CEO, joins "Bloomberg Tech" to talk about how Microsoft is helping the company reinvent itself through the use of agentic AI. He says the company is going from streaming music to streaming intelligence. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Spyware Targeted Serbian Protest Organizers’ Phones, Report Says
item.description: Spyware targeted Serbian student activists and politicians involved in anti-corruption protests against President Aleksandar Vucic ahead of local elections in March, a new report claimed.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Gallagher

item.title: Rockefeller Capital's Fleming Sees AI Driving Economic Optimism
item.description: Rockefeller Capital Management President and CEO Greg Fleming says the broader economy has reasons for optimism, led by artificial intelligence. Speaking on "Bloomberg Open Interest," Fleming also says he sees broad-based wealth creation in the US but expresses his concerns about the federal deficit. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Uber Cuts Jobs; Dell Raises Revenue Forecast | Stock Movers
item.description:
On this episode of Stock Movers:
- Uber Technologies (UBER) is cutting about 3,300 roles, or 10% of its staff globally, in a massive restructuring aimed at reducing management layers and reallocating spending into its ride-sharing, delivery and robotaxi businesses. - Dell Technologies (DELL) shares gain after the company’s second-quarter results beat expectations and it raised its full-year revenue forecast, supported by strong AI-related demand for its servers. - PG&E (PCG) plans to defer about $2 billion of investments next year as part of a strategic review of its businesses, a move that comes after it said a proposed revamp of California’s wildfire response didn’t do enough to protect the company and its peers from the cost of such disasters. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: AI Startup Wonderful Raises Funds at $5 Billion Valuation
item.description: Wonderful has closed a fundraising round that values the Israeli-Dutch startup, which builds software that coordinates artificial intelligence agents, at $5 billion.
item.dc:creator: Amy Thomson

item.title: Google Avoids Breakup as Judge Orders Ad Tech Unit Changes
item.description: Alphabet Inc.’s Google doesn’t have to sell off its advertising exchange and instead must make its ad tech tools work with those operated by rivals, a federal judge ruled Wednesday, in a move that saves the tech giant from a second bid to force a breakup.
item.dc:creator: Leah Nylen and Davey Alba

item.title: Upwind Raises $300 Million at $3.8 Billion Valuation for AI, Cloud Cybersecurity
item.description: Upwind Security, a startup offering cybersecurity for artificial intelligence and cloud applications, is raising fresh financing that values the company at $3.8 billion, according to people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Marissa Newman

item.title: Nvidia’s Huang Urges G20 to Speed AI Adoption, Spur Growth
item.description: Nvidia Corp. Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang called on Group of 20 nations to accelerate their adoption of artificial intelligence as a way to enhance growth, urging the world’s largest economies to expand data centers and other infrastructure to support the emerging technology.
item.dc:creator: Maggie Eastland

item.title: ElevenLabs Hires OpenAI VP as First Chief Revenue Officer
item.description: ElevenLabs has hired former OpenAI executive Ashley Kramer as its first chief revenue officer, part of the startup’s efforts to drum up business demand for its artificial intelligence voice tools.
item.dc:creator: Yazhou Sun

item.title: Uber to Cut 3,300 Jobs in Company Overhaul to Reduce Management Layers
item.description: Uber Technologies Inc. is cutting about 3,300 roles, or 10% of its staff globally, in a massive restructuring aimed at reducing management layers and reallocating spending into its ride-sharing, delivery and robotaxi businesses.
item.dc:creator: Natalie Lung

item.title: Kingspan Sells Green Bonds as Data Center Demand Lifts Firm
item.description: Kingspan Group Plc has raised €850 million ($985 million) from a two part green bond sale, as the AI data center build out has helped the Irish company lift its profit outlook.
item.dc:creator: Ronan Martin

item.title: Palo Alto Networks Shares Sink After Cloud Costs Shrink Margins
item.description: Palo Alto Networks Inc. slid by the most in almost seven months after the cybersecurity company said its shift to more software subscription products had increased cloud computing costs, pressuring gross margins.
item.dc:creator: Ignacio Gonzalez

item.title: Dell Shares Rise After Boosting Sales Outlook by $25 Billion
item.description: Dell Technologies Inc. shares jumped after the company boosted its annual sales forecast by $25 billion in a further sign of surging demand for servers to run artificial intelligence tasks.
